data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims reserves at the opening of 2022 were GBP 79.921m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle shows favourable development on underwriting years 2018-2020 totalling a gross release of GBP 12.635m (approximately 15.8% of opening gross claims outstanding). The syndicate also completed a Loss Portfolio Transfer (LPT) and Group Quota Share (QS) to MPMIC in 2022 which materially increased the reinsurers' share of reserves and resulted in deposits from reinsurers, although the LPT does not change gross reserves. Overall movement is accounted as a release driven by favourable claims development, with reinsurance activity affecting net positions.
raw_causal_phrases: The uncertainty within gross technical provisions is eliminated (apart from any bad debt consideration) by the LPT and QS contracts, reinsuring the balances to MPMIC.

Due to the current global inflationary pressures, an explicit allowance for future inflation has been added to the gross technical provisions. The loading was 3.4% on gross claims reserves (with no net impact).
An LPT and QS has been put into place reinsuring the loss reserves on the 2022 and prior years of account to MPMIC.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (PYD) was not reported as a single gross 'movement in prior year's provision' figure. PYD was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross cumulative estimates) by excluding the two most recent underwriting years (2021 and 2022) and summing the changes for 2018-2020. No explicit verbatim sentence stating the gross prior-year movement was found in the narrative; exact_reserve_text is therefore empty. The LPT/QS to MPMIC materially changed the reinsurers' share and produced deposits from reinsurers which affect net positions; this can distort interpretation of gross vs net movements if not considered. All amounts reported are in the report's native thousands converted to millions.
